Singulier x OMMAX are joining forces to build a leading European AI management consulting platform, combining deep strategic expertise with technology, data and AI capabilities. Together, we support clients across the full value creation journey, from strategy and due diligence through transformation and execution. 

We operate in a partner-led, entrepreneurial environment where everyone is expected to think critically, take ownership early and work directly with senior stakeholders.

As a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer, you will design, build and deploy AI, data and software solutions directly with our clients.

Work environment : engineering culture and stack 

We are building a small, highly skilled delivery team that shares engineering patterns and goes deep on a focused stack. Our aim is to make AI and technology transformation practical for mid-sized companies, within their budgets, teams and operating realities. Reusing proven foundations across projects lets us deliver faster, with consistent quality and a clear path to business value. 

The stack below is our default, not a constraint: we adapt to client environments and adopt new tools when the benefit is clear. 

  • Ways of working: Git, pull requests, code reviews, automated tests and CI/CD. Monitoring, evaluations and tracing ship with every AI application.

  • Data: PostgreSQL, DuckDB, LanceDB and Parquet, with attention to data quality, modelling and the simplest design that meets performance and scale needs. 
  • Infrastructure: infrastructure as code, Docker, and disciplined configuration, secrets and environment management. Databricks and Google Cloud, including BigQuery, when the workload calls for them.

Why join us 

  • Real impact, in production: what you build changes how our clients operate, and you see the results. 
  • Shape the practice early: join the delivery team while it is still small, and help set its stack, standards and reusable foundations. 
  • Ownership and variety: lead projects end to end across different industries and problems, working directly with business owners, investors and leadership teams.

Benefits

This is an opportunity to join a fast-growing, partner-led consulting platform at a pivotal moment in its development.

You will work on high-impact AI, Technology and Transformation engagements, advising private equity funds, portfolio companies and executive leadership teams on critical investment and transformation decisions.

As Singulier x OMMAX build a leading European AI management consulting platform, you will help shape how AI, technology, data and business strategy come together to create lasting value for clients.

You will also benefit from significant exposure to Technology Due Diligence, Value Creation and Transformation projects, a steep learning curve, early ownership, close mentorship and the opportunity to contribute to the growth of an entrepreneurial consulting firm operating at European scale.

This includes taking ownership of configuration, access management, operational reliability, governance, documentation, and cost control.

We need someone who can identify issues, propose practical improvements, coordinate implementation, and verify that our systems continue to work reliably. You should be comfortable combining hands-on technical work with project management, team leadership, mentoring, and coordination of outsourced specialists.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain AI assistants and agents using Microsoft Copilot Studio and Microsoft Foundry.
  • Identify practical opportunities for Microsoft 365 Copilot and help teams use it effectively.

  • Translate business requirements into clear tasks, delivery milestones, and verifiable acceptance criteria.
  • Manage project scope, priorities, dependencies, risks, and stakeholder communication.
  • Coordinate outsourced developers, review their deliverables, and maintain clear ownership.
  • Mentor colleagues through practical demonstrations, reviews, and knowledge transfer.
  • Keep solutions maintainable and proportionate to the problem and startup budget.

Required Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience delivering production solutions using Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry, and Power Automate.
  • Practical understanding of Microsoft 365 Copilot and its use in business workflows.
  • Experience building AI agents or assistants connected to business data, tools, and APIs.
  • Experience evaluating AI-generated answers and actions, including handling unreliable or unsupported output.

  • Experience integrating SharePoint, Teams, Dataverse, Microsoft Graph, or comparable business platforms.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Entra ID, application permissions, authentication, and secure credential handling.

  • Proven experience independently administering a company's Microsoft environment, with responsibility for reliable operation and ongoing improvement.
  • Hands-on experience configuring and managing Power Platform solutions connected to GitHub.
  • Practical experience with GitHub Actions or comparable CI/CD workflows for Microsoft solutions.

Especially Valuable Experience

  • Delivering Microsoft AI or automation projects in a startup or consulting environment.
  • Building retrieval workflows with documented knowledge sources and permission-aware access.
  • Working with Power Apps, Azure services, SQL databases, or Azure DevOps.
  • Experience with Azure API Management and its AI gateway capabilities, including authentication, model routing, usage limits, monitoring, and cost control.
  • Experience with related components such as Azure Key Vault, Azure Monitor, Application Insights, and Azure AI Search.
  • Experience building and maintaining Power BI reports and dashboards, including Power Query, data modelling, DAX, scheduled refresh, workspace permissions, and row-level security.
  • Experience connecting reporting and analytics to operational workflows and business decisions.
  • Replacing fragile workflows with solutions that are easier to operate and maintain.
  • Coordinating outsourced implementation while retaining internal technical ownership.
  • Using AI development tools effectively and recognizing when generated solutions introduce unnecessary complexity.

Growth, Leadership and CompensationThis is an opportunity to join early and help shape our Microsoft AI and automation practice.

Initial compensation will reflect our startup budget, your experience, and the agreed responsibilities. As the business develops and your contribution grows, we aim to offer substantial salary progression during the first few years.

Strong contributors may progress into roles such as Microsoft AI Team Lead, AI & Automation Lead, Solutions Architect, or Head of AI & Automation. Progression will depend on demonstrated results, leadership capability, company growth, and financial capacity. We will discuss expectations and progression milestones openly during recruitment.

Nous recherchons un Ingénieur Principal capable d’évoluer au-delà des frontières d’une équipe ou d’une discipline technique.

Référent technique transverse, il est un interlocuteur naturel vers qui l’on se tourne lorsqu’un problème est complexe, qu’un sujet traverse plusieurs domaines ou qu’une idée doit vite devenir réalité.

En lien direct avec le CTO et les départements techniques, il a une vision globale des enjeux techniques et de l’entreprise, tout en restant résolument hands-on.

La mission

L’Ingénieur Principal intervient sur des sujets variés et transverses : IA, logiciel, interface et parcours utilisateur, infrastructure, cybersécurité, architecture, données, produit, métier, nouvelles technologies, etc.

Il est amené à :

  • Transformer un problème mal défini, une idée ou un besoin en solution concrète, du prototype à la production ;

  • Proposer et challenger les choix techniques, en pesant risques, dépendances, opportunités, délais et coûts ;

  • Veiller à la bonne évolution et au maintien en conditions opérationnelles des solutions ;

  • Identifier les défauts et les axes d’amélioration, quelle qu’en soit la nature ;

  • Contribuer au respect des engagements réglementaires et contractuels de l’entreprise ainsi qu’à l’obtention et au maintien de ses certifications (ISO, etc.) ;

  • Échanger directement avec les clients pour comprendre leurs besoins, clarifier les problèmes rencontrés et concevoir des solutions adaptées ;

  • Être le relais du CTO sur les sujets techniques transverses.

La posture

Très réactif, il sait réévaluer ses priorités et se mobiliser rapidement lorsqu’un sujet important ou critique le nécessite. Il prend un sujet dans son ensemble, du problème à la mise en production, sans perdre de vue la finalité : qui va l’utiliser, quel problème cela résout, à quoi ressemble une solution réellement utile. Il n’hésite pas à solliciter les bons interlocuteurs et à rechercher les ressources nécessaires pour faire avancer les sujets.

Il sait passer de la réflexion à l’exécution et accorde autant d’importance à la compréhension du besoin qu’à l’excellence du résultat.

Face à un sujet critique, il agit comme une force spéciale d’intervention : il cerne et extrapole vite les enjeux d’un problème parfois à peine défini, pense un coup d’avance sans surconstruire, décide et construit lui-même la solution, tout en gardant une vision d’ensemble.

Nous recherchons avant tout un développeur exceptionnel, capable de comprendre rapidement des problèmes complexes, de concevoir des solutions pertinentes et de les concrétiser avec pragmatisme.

TL;DR:
We’re looking for a full-stack engineer obsessed with Lovable’s growth engine - turning first touches into daily habits, and daily habits into a thriving ecosystem and real revenue. One sprint you’re shipping onboarding and activation flows; the next you’re crafting distribution rails and monetization features that help builders reach more users and keep them around. You think in React and APIs, but your first instinct is always: does this make users more successful, more often?

Coding skills + excellent taste + growth instincts + product obsession = you.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What we’re looking for

  • 5+ years of experience building and growing user-facing products in high-performing teams, ideally including growth work, marketplaces/platforms, or communities.

  • Strong product sense and UX taste for multi-sided systems with creators, learners, and customers - you can see problems from multiple sides and design for all of them.

  • Comfortable using data, funnels, analytics, attribution, and A/B testing to shape what you build and how you iterate.

  • Skilled at designing, measuring, and iterating experiments, and thorough in setting up growth systems “right” from the start.

  • Experience collaborating across functions (design, marketing, partnerships, support, data) to launch and grow new product surfaces and ecosystems.

  • Enjoys designing reusable growth, ecosystem, and monetization tools that other builders can plug into, with a pragmatic and detail-oriented mindset.

  • Motivated by helping others succeed and by seeing impact through engagement, measurable results, and revenue - you care about the scoreboard as much as the code.

What you’ll do

In one sentence: You will build the growth, ecosystem, and monetization systems that make Lovable - and the apps built on it - sticky, discoverable, and revenue-generating.

  • Ship and iterate activation, monetization and retention experiences that create fast, repeatable value and turn first-time users into long-term fans.

  • Build distribution rails for user apps: SEO and performance, shareable moments, social previews, email and lifecycle journeys, and other growth hooks.

  • Ship marketplace and ecosystem features for publishing, discovering, and reusing apps, templates, components, and services - plus profiles, reviews, and matching between builders and customers.

  • Design and implement monetization and pricing flows: payments, subscriptions, access control, plans, paywalls, billing integration, and revenue-share models that work for creators, customers, and Lovable.

  • Build the analytics and experimentation foundations - events, funnels, attribution, and A/B tests - so the team can understand what works and double down on it.

  • Collaborate closely with design, marketing, partnerships, and support to launch and grow new surfaces across the product and ecosystem.

  • Keep the experience relentlessly Lovable while making growth the engine, not the afterthought.

Our tech stack

We're building with tools that both humans and AI love:

  • Frontend: React

  • Backend: Golang and Rust

  • Cloud: Cloudflare, GCP, AWS, Many LLM providers

  • DevOps & Tooling: Github Actions, Grafana, OTEL, infra-as-code (Terraform)

About your application

Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.

We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

Our founders have built successful companies before, including alongside several of the people now at Motion. A number of teammates chose to build again here — a reflection of the trust, culture, and conviction behind what we’re building.

The people building Motion are deeply embedded in where AI and our industry is heading, and obsessed with closing the gap between what's possible and what's actually shipping in product. We're a 75 person remote team backed by $65M+ in funding with a valuation that's nearly 3x'd in under two years. If you want to work on a hard problem, with people who've done it before, and a product that customers genuinely love - we'd love to connect!

▶️ Brief overview of the Motion product & Runneth from our Co-Founder & CEO, Reza Khadjavi.

The Role

Motion’s products increasingly rely on data-intensive APIs. Beyond our reporting platform, MCP server, and public endpoints, these APIs now power per-customer environments where AI systems can execute tasks, access customer-specific state, and proactively run analysis. Today, that means Azure VMs running Dockerized workloads and a growing layer of application code which needs to cover everything from functionality to routine updates.

We’re looking for a senior software engineer who loves working at the boundary between product code and infrastructure. This is not a traditional DevOps or SRE role. You’ll spend most of your time writing application code that controls infrastructure primitives: messaging queue abstractions, VM management, data lifecycle, container updates, no-downtime migrations, bootstrapping, permissions, observability, and security.

The right person is comfortable going deep into Linux, containers, networking, and all that jazz, but thinks like a product engineer: shipping reliable systems, choosing pragmatic abstractions, and making complicated runtime behavior feel routine to our customers.

| Our tech stack: Node.js, TypeScript, React, MongoDB, ElasticSearch, Azure, and Pulumi.

  • 🔗 Explore our Engineering at Motion page to learn more about our team, our work, and how we build together.
  • 👩‍💻 Browse our Engineering Blog for an inside look at the decisions our team is making, the things we're learning, and what it means for us to be building an AI product today.

What You'd Be Doing 🛠️

  • Build and evolve the systems that provision, update, secure, and observe Motion’s agent environments.
  • Design abstractions around queues, locks, background tasks, and service bus mechanics so product engineers can build on reliable primitives.
  • Evolve our infrastructure-as-code footprint in Pulumi — defining patterns other engineers can build on.
  • Work with Linux systems, mounted persistent storage, OS disks, container boundaries, permissions, logs, and runtime debugging.
  • Participate in a small, high-ownership, cross-functional team with weekly cycles.

Our ideal fit brings ✨

  • 6+ years of experience as a software engineer, with meaningful time spent going deep into infrastructure.
  • Strong production backend experience. TypeScript / Node.js is ideal, but we care more about strong engineering judgment and the ability to learn our stack quickly
  • Deep, hands-on cloud experience. Azure is where we live, but AWS or GCP experience transfers if you are strong on the fundamentals.
  • Fluency with infrastructure-as-code. We use Pulumi but any relevant experience in Terraform or CDK is good.
  • Hands-on experience with containers and runtime environments. Docker is important; experience with Kubernetes, Nomad, ECS, Docker Swarm, or similar orchestration systems is helpful but not required.
  • Experience designing reliable systems around background jobs, queues, locks, service buses, migrations, retries, and failure recovery.
  • Strong security instincts for application runtime environments.
  • and you'll be a strong fit if you align with these qualities:
  • You're genuinely excited about infrastructure. When something breaks, you want to understand how the system actually works, not just scale and restart it.
  • A strong sense of ownership: you make decisions and move quickly to fix things quickly when they go wrong.
  • A pragmatic mindset. You can ship the simple thing when speed matters, while flagging that which needs to evolve later.
  • Comfortable in a fast-moving startup where requirements come with ambiguity and the “right” way isn't handed to you.
  • You enjoy being a strong individual contributor and a supportive teammate. Engineering is a team sport here 💪

What You'll Love About Motion 💜

  • Competitive compensation package: We offer competitive compensation, including equity for all employees, health benefits from day one, a monthly health & lifestyle stipend to support your well-being, 20 days of PTO, and a $1,500 work-from-home stipend.
  • Remote-first with hybrid flexibility: We're a remote-first company with team members spanning Canada, the U.S., and beyond, but also have office spaces in 4 main hubs (Toronto, Montreal, Vancouver, and Porto) for optional hybrid work.
  • Growth that speaks for itself: Motion has strong product-market fit, 2.5x YoY growth, second-time founders with deep industry knowledge, and $30M in Series B funding to fuel our momentum.
  • Opportunity for impact: As an early team member, your contributions will directly shape the product, team, and the future of the company. If you're excited about building, you’ll thrive here!
  • Award-winning team: We're a low-ego, high-performing team that was just ranked #19 on G2's list of Best Canadian Software Companies for 2026.
  • Team connection:
    • Virtual: Day-to-day, we use Roam, an AI-powered virtual office platform that fosters spontaneous collaboration, drop into meetings or quick chats, and interact with colleagues for a simulated, "live" digital headquarters.
    • In-person: Outside of the option to go to one of our offices, our team gets together in-person for a week every two months, and we have a company retreat every summer.
We closed out 2024 with a $30M Series B raise and strong signals from our customers. In 2025, we built the foundational capabilities our customers rely on, setting the stage for what's to come. In 2026, with fresh funding ($65M+ total capital raised), we’re building forward from that foundation, taking what we learned to market in a deeply AI-native way.

Compliance remains one of the most manual functions in financial services. While most institutions still rely on fragmented tools and human-driven workflows, we believe AI is enabling a fundamental shift toward autonomous compliance. You’ll join an AI-native engineering team where AI is central to how we design, build and ship software. We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer who understands software deeply, uses AI to build better software faster, and wants to help improve how the whole team works.

You will own projects from understanding the customer problem to shipping a solution and improving it in production. Working closely with engineering and product, you will help decide what we build, how we build it, and where to invest as the platform grows.

We value engineers who bring depth in their area and curiosity beyond it.

  • Contribute to the evolution of our platform as we build more AI-powered compliance capabilities.

  • You have 5+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of delivering and maintaining software in production.

  • You want to help shape an AI-native engineering team. You enjoy improving how software gets built, from reusable agent workflows to better testing and feedback loops, and turning your own discoveries into practices that make the whole team more effective.

  • Join a company with traction and room to shape its future. With 100+ financial institutions using Dotfile and a recent Series A, you’ll help define the next stage of the product and engineering team.

Depuis notre création en 2020, nous sommes devenus un acteur reconnu du numérique responsable en France :

  • Labellisés GreenTech Innovation (label du Ministère de la Transition Écologique) et inscrits dans l'Économie Sociale et Solidaire (ESS)
  • Sélectionnés par le Mouvement Impact France dans son classement Impact 120
  • Une équipe de 35 expertes engagées, aux côtés de plusieurs clients

Nos Activités

  • Fruggr, notre solution SaaS, une plateforme qui permet aux entreprises de piloter leur performance ESG IT, leur accessibilité numérique et leur gouvernance de l'IA.
  • Transformation sur les usages de l'IA, nous aidons les entreprises à déployer une intelligence artificielle responsable, maîtrisée et conforme aux exigences réglementaires (AI Act…).
  • Développement web, mobile et applicatif responsable, nous concevons des solutions numériques durables, accessibles et inclusives.

Description Du Poste

Le poste

Vous rejoignez l'équipe produit de Fruggr, à Nantes. Vous y développez les fonctionnalités de Fruggr, notre plateforme SaaS : gouvernance de l'IA, accessibilité numérique et Digital Workplace.

Ce qu'on attend de vous, ce n'est pas d'écrire le plus de lignes de code possible. C'est de résoudre les bons problèmes, avec les bons outils et avec l'équipe. Chez nous, travailler avec quelqu'un, c'est travailler avec deux interlocuteurs : la personne et son IA. Vous savez parler aux deux.

Concrètement, l'IA fait partie de notre méthode de travail quotidienne : vous écrivez les specs, l'agent code, vous validez, vous livrez. Et vous challengez les choix de la machine pour tirer le meilleur de ce binôme.

Vos activités au quotidien

  • Comprendre le besoin d'une PO ou d'un client et le traduire en spécifications claires, exploitables par l'équipe et par ses agents IA.
  • Concevoir, développer et faire évoluer les fonctionnalités du produit, en choisissant la technologie la plus adaptée au problème posé.
  • Travailler au quotidien avec des outils d'IA (Claude Code, Spec-Driven Development, harnais de développement), en gardant un regard critique sur ce que produit la machine.
  • Aider vos collègues à tirer le meilleur de l'IA dans leur façon de travailler : partager vos pratiques, débloquer les situations, rendre les choses simples.
  • Participer au support produit en rotation avec les autres développeureuses : investiguer, diagnostiquer et résoudre les incidents remontés par les clients.
  • Contribuer aux choix d'architecture et à la qualité de la plateforme.

L'environnement technique

Le produit tourne aujourd'hui principalement en TypeScript (Node.js, React), avec du GraphQL, sur Azure.

Vous ne maîtrisez pas ces technologies ? Ce n'est pas un prérequis. Avec l'IA, le langage devient un outil parmi d'autres : ce qui compte, c'est votre expérience du développement et votre capacité à choisir la bonne techno selon le contexte. Vous venez de .NET, de Java, de Python ou d'ailleurs et vous avez envie d'élargir votre horizon ? Votre candidature nous intéresse.

Profil recherché

  • Au moins 3 ans d'expérience en développement, avec plusieurs projets menés de bout en bout.
  • Un vrai bagage de développeureuse : vous avez pratiqué plusieurs langages ou environnements et savez justifier vos choix techniques.
  • Une pratique concrète de l'IA dans votre travail de développement. Pas besoin d'être experte, mais vous savez ce qu'est le Spec-Driven Development ou un harnais de développement, et vous connaissez les forces et les limites de ces outils.
  • Une expérience dans un contexte produit est un vrai plus : vous comprenez en quoi les enjeux diffèrent de ceux d'un projet en prestation.
  • Un grand sens de la pédagogie. Vous savez vulgariser, vous adapter à votre interlocuteur et expliquer un sujet technique à quelqu'un qui n'est pas développeur.
  • Un esprit d'équipe affirmé. Vous êtes proactifve face aux problèmes et vous préférez avancer avec les autres plutôt que seule dans votre coin.
  • L'envie de faire partie de la vie de l'équipe nantaise, avec une présence dans nos locaux 2 à 3 jours par semaine.

Vous ne cochez pas toutes les cases mais le poste vous parle ? Certaines compétences s'acquièrent en chemin : n'hésitez pas à postuler.

Démarrage

Pas d'urgence : si vous avez un préavis de 3 mois, ce n'est pas un problème.

Process de recrutement

  • Un premier échange RH pour parler de votre parcours, de vos motivations et de vos attentes.
  • Un entretien technique avec un membre de l'équipe : vos expériences, votre façon de travailler avec l'IA et votre approche des problèmes.
  • Un entretien avec une responsable de l'activité

Avantages

  • Télétravail

WHY THIS ROLE, NOW


Vocca is 2 years old. Our AI answers the phone for medical practices so they never miss a patient call again, and it already handles 70% of calls without a human. Revenue grew 3x in the last 6 months and we are opening the US. The product works. The next 12 months are about scaling it, and a call only counts as handled if the appointment lands in the clinic's software. That is this role.


THE PROBLEM YOU WILL SOLVE


Every medical practice runs on software that holds its calendar and its patients. There are dozens of different ones. Most were built twenty years ago and some have no API at all. To book an appointment during a call, our AI agent has to read and write in that software in real time, while the patient waits on the line. Nobody else has managed to build this. On several of these systems, Vocca is the only integrator in the world.

This is the work with the most direct impact on the business. A clinic whose software is connected to our agent does not switch. Retention, pricing power, our lead over competitors: it all depends on these integrations. Every software we cannot connect is a clinic we cannot sign.

The next step is writing back. Today the agent reads and books. Tomorrow it updates records in EHR, PMS and RIS systems, which raises the reliability bar a lot. In the US, we are opening the dental software ecosystem, with the compliance work that comes with it (HIPAA, SOC2).

The long term vision is simple: the agent becomes the action layer between patients and everything the front desk used to do by hand. The integrations are the road to get there. You would be building that road.


WHAT YOU WILL OWN


  • The architecture of our booking layer. Today it is code written provider by provider, under pressure. It is becoming one unified layer in TypeScript that can handle the rules of each medical centre and where adding a new software takes days, not weeks.
  • Speed and reliability at more than 1 million calls a month. A call to a clinic software can take several seconds, and the patient cannot wait. You decide how we detect a booking failure in a clinic within 24 hours and what a healthy integration looks like.
  • The hard integrations that nobody else wants to do. They are what makes Vocca hard to replace.
  • The decisions on your scope. You decide which software we connect first, with the sales, ops and support teams and the clinics themselves, and you prove it worked with a number: bookings that go through, failures caught, clinics signed.
  • The next hires. You take part in hiring the engineers who join after you, and you help them ship in their first week.


HOW WE BUILD


  • We are experimental, not R&D. You test, you prove with data, you ship. Challenging a decision means coming back with a number.
  • We ship the version that works, then fix the last 1% when it shows up. With AI, this trade off is much cheaper than before. But the judgment about what not to touch is yours.
  • We use AI seriously. Agents in every workflow, Claude Max provided. A migration estimated at 3 months was done in 2 weeks.
  • You talk every day with the ops team that deploys clinics, the support team that hears when something breaks and, when it matters, the clinics and the software vendors themselves.


STACK


TypeScript everywhere (Node, monorepo), PostgreSQL, REST and SOAP APIs from software vendors. We are migrating our last Python services to TypeScript over the coming months.


WHO DOES WELL HERE


  • You have built something that mattered: an early engineer at a startup that took off, a founding engineer, a system you launched that real users depended on. You can tell us who it was for, what problem it solved and which number moved.
  • You have integrated systems you did not control and you know the difference between a clean API and the real world.
  • 4+ years building backend systems in production, mostly in startups or fast growing companies where you had to decide with incomplete information.
  • Strong in TypeScript and Node. Or a strong backend engineer in Go, Python or Java who is clearly ready to become strong in TypeScript.
  • Solid engineering habits: system design, clean refactoring and a good nose for the risks of generated code that nobody tested.
  • You can say no, reduce the scope and explain a technical decision to a founder in two minutes.


WHAT WE EXPECT FROM YOU


First week

  • Get onboarded on the stack.
  • Ship your first fix on a live integration.

First month

  • Own one integration end to end, from the software vendor to production, and show what it changed.
  • Write down how our booking layer should evolve.

First 3 months

  • The unified booking layer in TypeScript is the standard.
  • Adding a new software takes days, not weeks.
  • We detect a booking failure in any clinic within 24 hours.

6 to 12 months

  • Our first US integrations run in production.
  • You have hired at least one engineer and they ship on their own.


PROCESS: 4 STEPS, FAST


  1. 45 min with Nans (Talent).
  2. 30 min with Hugo (CTO) or Pierrick (Head of Engineering).
  3. 1h30 in our office: live coding without AI, a real conversation about architecture and a product case with Charles, our CPO.
  4. 30 min with the one you have not met yet.


Then references and an offer. When the match is obvious, we have made an offer in 24 hours. You get feedback at every step.


PRACTICAL

  • Paris, rue d'Alexandrie (Sentier), new offices.
  • Salary : 70-100K + BSPCE.
  • Hybrid 3 days at the office.
  • Claude Max provided.

And a black-belt prompter. I mean that as a level, not a flourish. The tell: if you watch other developers work in AI environments and feel real frustration — everyone prompts, most prompt badly — and you have quietly built your own standing rule files, your own context discipline, your own reusable prompt library, then you already know what I am describing. That is the rarer of the two skills, and the one I weight hardest.

Under the product, 60+ specialist agents run continuous extraction over each customer's documents and sessions into a persistent, per-company memory: every fact dated and traced to its source sentence, contradictions kept rather than overwritten — a discipline we call Total Capture. Patent-pending since July, in context engineering.

Stack: TypeScript throughout. A NestJS API plus a separate NestJS worker on Railway, Next.js 16 / React 19 on Vercel, Postgres with Prisma, Redis and BullMQ, Pinecone, S3-compatible storage. Agents are LangChain.js / LangGraph ReAct agents on Anthropic Claude across three model tiers, with OpenAI embeddings. Every prompt body and model config lives in one versioned master file synced to LangSmith, never hardcoded in TypeScript.

That was the environment, not me: 45 interconnected instruction files deploying sub-agents, around 300,000 words of standing rules, orchestrated by one always-on kernel that classifies each session, auto-attaches the rules matching the files being touched, and generates sub-agentic plans for the work.

Ce poste ouvrira officiellement en septembre, mais on préfère prendre de l’avance !

Boond est en train de Scale ! 🦊

Boond, c’est la plateforme SaaS qui booste la performance des ESN et cabinets de conseil. On accompagne 2000 clients, ESN, cabinets de conseil et sociétés d’ingénierie, et près de 100 000 utilisateurs en France et à l’international.

Le tout en 100% remote et ça depuis 2009, avec aujourd’hui, 110 Boonders 🦊

Aujourd’hui : 13M€ d’ARR, 21M€ d’ici 24 mois. On a prouvé que l’on savait scaler intelligemment en gardant notre rentabilité et notre culture.

Et Boond, c’est avant tout une boîte de tech, créée par un tech, Tanguy. Ici, on aime le code bien pensé et les équipes qui avancent ensemble. On grandit, et on renforce plusieurs de nos squads avec des Senior Dev Fullstack.

Un mot honnête sur le métier : avec l’arrivée des assistants de code IA, la valeur d’un·e dev se déplace de l’écriture de code vers la réflexion métier : comprendre les règles produit, challenger une spec, savoir quoi construire et pourquoi.

Et pour ça, on a besoin de toi !

La (shiny) team 🏆 :

Chez Boond, tout tourne autour des squads produits 🙌

Une squad type, c’est un noyau resserré : un Product Owner, une QA attitrée (incollable sur les règles de gestion), un·e Designer attitré·e, plusieurs devs Fullstack (dont des Seniors) et un Lead Dev qui anime le tout. En transverse, tu peux compter sur Baloo (Principal Engineer, référent technique de la tribu) et Florens (Engineering Manager, ton futur manager).

On travaille en Shape-Up : par trimestres, avec des sprints de 2 semaines de Delivery, puis un Cool Down en fin de trimestre pour la veille, l’expérimentation et le refacto 🔥

Grow, par exemple, c’est une squad très exposée UX, la porte d’entrée produit pour les utilisateurs Boond. Une équipe soudée, qui a tenu sous pression sans se déchirer, où les devs sont embarqués tôt dans le shaping et où les décisions Produit / Design / Tech se prennent ensemble ❤️

Voici ton (futur) terrain de jeu :

Ton quotidien, c’est environ 65% de règles métier / droits et 35% d’archi / technique : traduire des contraintes ESN complexes en code robuste. Réparti comme ça :

🛠 Conception — ~ 40%

  • Tu participes aux shapings avec le PO, tu es force de proposition sur les sujets à venir.

  • Tu es problem-solver sur les règles de droits : chez nous elles sont riches et complexes (beaucoup de personas, beaucoup de métiers), et c’est un vrai terrain de jeu.

💻 Développement — ~35%

  • Tu développes les features, tu refactos, tu optimises le cache, tu stabilises les tests.

  • Tu aides la team Core/Architecte à faire évoluer la stack.

🤝 Transverse — ~20%

  • KPIs cross-squads, mise à dispo de data, Justice League (coup de main au support), cérémonies (daily, weekly, tres amigos dev/QA/PO, kick-off, REX).

🔭 Veille — ~10%

  • Cool Down, expérimentation, contribution au BoondGame technique

Ta stack 🧰

  • Back : monolithe PHP 8.2 sur Fat-Free Framework + notre surcouche maison, RabbitMQ, MariaDB, SolR

  • Front : Ember Octane 4.12 (montée de version en continu)

  • CI / Infra : Jenkins, Cypress, GitLab CI et Docker / K8s en cours de déploiement

  • Outils : Claude code, Git, Jira, Confluence, Slack, PHPStorm, MacOS

Un chiffre pour la route : certains clients ont jusqu’à 800 000 candidats en base. Le moindre changement d’API peut coûter des millisecondes… multipliées par des imports de masse. La perf, c’est une vigilance permanente ⚡

  • Le mur d’entrée. Legacy métier dense + patterns du framework maison (des conventions absentes de Laravel/Symfony).

  • Des données du monde réel. Le modèle est permissif : un champ peut être laissé vide ou renseigné de travers. On code donc pour le monde réel, celui où l’utilisateur ne suit pas toujours le chemin qu’on avait prévu, pas seulement pour le scénario idéal.

  • Des évolutions à fort enjeu. Faire évoluer la structure de données d’un produit utilisé chaque jour par des milliers d’entreprises, ça se prépare : les migrations lourdes se testent en préprod avant d’être jouées, et on avance avec méthode plutôt qu’en force.

  • Ember.js, c’est niche. Peu connu en France mais stable et rétrocompatible (LTS).

Si ces points t’intriguent plus qu’ils ne te font fuir, c’est très bon signe 😏

  • 8 ans+ en dev web sur des produits complexes (ni junior, ni profil qui n’a fait que du CRUD).

  • À l’aise dans le legacy : tu as évolué dans un monolithe dense, tu cartographies avant d’agir, tu gères le couplage fort et les données imparfaites sans paniquer.

  • Appétence métier réelle : tu prends du plaisir sur les règles de gestion, pas seulement sur l’archi.

  • 🦊 Le petit + : tu viens d’un éditeur SaaS B2B à règles métier fortes — ERP / gestion / RH, fintech / paiement, ou ATS / CRM. Tu arrives avec le bon réflexe métier.
